kid.question: Which three things does Micah say the Lord requires?

options.text: Do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God
Seek wisdom, keep promises, and teach children about God
Speak kindly, give freely, and remember the ancient covenant
Show courage, endure trials, and pray each morning to God

kid.explanation: The verse names justice, love of mercy, and humble walking with God as the Lord's requirements.

kid.question: Which tools are used dishonestly in Micah's accusation?

options.text: Plows and sickles
Nets and fishing lines
Scales and weights
Chisels and hammers

kid.explanation: Micah names scant measures, wicked balances, and deceitful weights among the city's wrongs.

kid.question: What will happen when the people sow their crops?

options.text: They will sell the firstfruits
They will trade the harvest
They will share the produce
They will not reap them

kid.explanation: Judgment includes sowing without reaping and producing oil and wine without enjoying them.

kid.question: To whom does Micah say he will look and wait?

options.text: The ruler of his country
The God of his salvation
The judge of his city
The guide of his household

kid.explanation: Amid the breakdown of trust, Micah looks to the Lord and waits for the God of his salvation.

kid.question: What will the Lord be when Micah sits in darkness?

options.text: A light to him
A shield around him
A road before him
A wall beside him

kid.explanation: Micah expresses hope that when he sits in darkness the Lord will be a light to him.

kid.question: What does Micah acknowledge as he bears the Lord's anger?

options.text: He has ignored a message from the king
He has spoken falsely about his neighbors
He has withheld an offering from the priests
He has sinned against the Lord

kid.explanation: Micah acknowledges his own sin as he bears indignation and looks ahead to the Lord pleading his cause.

kid.question: What picture describes God removing His people's sins?

options.text: Blowing them across the desert sand
Burning them on the temple altar
Casting them into the sea's depths
Burying them beneath the mountain stones

kid.explanation: The promise describes compassion, subdued iniquities, and sins cast into the depths of the sea.

kid.question: Whose old promises does Micah say God will keep?

options.text: Jacob's and Abraham's
Moses's and Aaron's
David's and Solomon's
Elijah's and Elisha's

kid.explanation: Micah closes with God's truth to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, sworn to the fathers from old times.

kid.question: Which city is named at the beginning of Nahum?

options.text: Babylon
Nineveh
Jerusalem
Samaria

kid.explanation: Nahum's opening identifies the burden as concerning Nineveh.

kid.question: What picture describes the Lord in a day of trouble?

options.text: A vineyard
A fountain
A stronghold
A shepherd

kid.explanation: Nahum calls the Lord good and a stronghold in trouble, knowing those who trust in Him.

high-school.question: Which behaviors accompany the deceitful weights in Micah's indictment?

options.text: Refusal of hospitality and neglect of the widowed families
Violence among the rich and lying among the inhabitants
Judges taking bribes and priests withholding the required offerings
Soldiers robbing travelers and rulers confiscating the inherited fields

high-school.explanation: The requirement to do justly is followed by accusations of scant measures, deceitful weights, violence, and lies.

high-school.question: What common frustration unites the announced losses in Micah 6:14-15?

options.text: Eating brings sickness, sowing attracts thieves, and pressing supplies the invading royal household
Eating is forbidden, sowing is delayed, and pressing is reserved for the sanctuary priests
Eating brings no satisfaction, sowing no reaping, and pressing no enjoyment of produce
Eating exhausts supplies, sowing increases debts, and pressing damages the remaining storage jars

high-school.explanation: Eating brings no satisfaction, sowing no harvest, and pressing olives or grapes no enjoyment of their products.

high-school.question: What social condition does the search for missing fruit picture in Micah 7?

options.text: Upright people have disappeared amid violence
Food sellers have abandoned markets during a siege
Farm workers have refused to gather the first harvest
Returning captives have replanted the land with grain

high-school.explanation: The longing for a fruit cluster leads into the lament that good and upright people have perished and that men hunt one another.

high-school.question: What contrast follows the warnings about friends and family?

options.text: Distrust among people gives way to escape toward Egypt
Conflict among families gives way to loyalty toward a new king
Conflict among families gives way to confidence in city defenses
Distrust among people gives way to waiting on God

high-school.explanation: After warnings about close relationships, the speaker declares he will look to the Lord, wait, and be heard.

high-school.question: How can the speaker confess sin and still answer an enemy's rejoicing?

options.text: He expects the priests to prove he has been falsely accused
He expects the king to transfer his penalty to the enemy
He expects the Lord to bring him from darkness to light
He expects the judges to dismiss the charge before hearing evidence

high-school.explanation: He acknowledges sin and indignation but expects the Lord to plead his cause and bring him into light.

high-school.question: Which earlier deliverance sets the pattern for promised wonders?

options.text: The return from Babylon
The departure from Egypt
The victory at Jericho
The escape from Nineveh

high-school.explanation: The Lord promises marvelous things according to the days of coming out of Egypt.

high-school.question: What reason does Micah give for the Lord not retaining anger forever?

options.text: He accepts the city's tribute
He delights in mercy
He answers the priests' intercession
He honors the people's sacrifices

high-school.explanation: The passage grounds the end of retained anger in God's delight in mercy and willingness to pardon.

high-school.question: How are God's truth and mercy assigned in Micah's final promise?

options.text: Truth to Jacob and mercy to Abraham
Truth to Moses and mercy to Aaron
Truth to David and mercy to Solomon
Truth to Isaac and mercy to Joseph

high-school.explanation: Pardon and compassion culminate in sins cast into the sea and truth and mercy sworn to Jacob and Abraham.

high-school.question: Which qualities does Nahum name alongside the refusal to acquit the wicked?

options.text: Faithfulness to covenants and concern for the poor
Knowledge of hidden things and wisdom in counsel
Abundance in mercy and readiness to forgive
Slowness to anger and greatness in power

high-school.explanation: Nahum names slowness to anger and great power while expressly denying acquittal of the wicked.

high-school.question: Who is explicitly named as known by the Lord in the stronghold promise?

options.text: Those who trust in Him
Those who come to His temple
Those who bring Him their offerings
Those who teach His people the law

high-school.explanation: The stronghold for those trusting Him stands alongside flood and darkness in the announced judgment.

expert.question: How does Micah 6:8-12 move from requirement to accusation?

options.text: Justice, mercy, and humility precede charges of neglected feasts, sacrifices, and vows
Fasting, sacrifice, and pilgrimage precede charges of dishonest measures, violence, and lies
Justice, mercy, and humility precede charges of dishonest measures, violence, and lies
Fasting, sacrifice, and pilgrimage precede charges of neglected feasts, sacrifices, and vows

expert.explanation: Justice, mercy, and humility provide the standard against which false measures, violence, and lying stand condemned.

expert.question: What does the naming of Omri and Ahab add to the judgment oracle?

options.text: The people perpetuate condemned royal patterns and counsels
The people await returning monarchs to restore the covenant
The people reject royal statutes in favor of new foreign customs
The people seek royal approval before surrendering their houses

expert.explanation: Keeping Omri's statutes and Ahab's works, and walking in their counsels, is connected with desolation and reproach.

expert.question: How does the harvest lament become a judgment about human character?

options.text: Abundance of spoiled fruit leads into rejection of foreign trade
Delay of the grape harvest leads into a demand for fairer wages
Division of the summer harvest leads into a call for royal arbitration
Absence of desired fruit leads into absence of the upright

expert.explanation: The speaker cannot find a cluster or first-ripe fruit, then laments the disappearance of good people and the thornlike character of those remaining.

expert.question: What stance accompanies the speaker's expectation of vindication?

options.text: He denies the accusation and awaits God's exposure of false witnesses
He admits sin and bears indignation while awaiting God's defense
He promises a new offering and awaits God's acceptance of the gift
He recalls earlier obedience and awaits God's rejection of the charge

expert.explanation: Trust that God will hear and bring light includes an explicit confession of sin and acceptance of indignation.

expert.question: How does the shepherding petition connect heritage with restoration?

options.text: The Lord is asked to restore His appointed guards to their former boundary stations
The Lord is asked to return His scattered merchants to their former trading routes
The Lord is asked to bring His surviving armies to their former royal fortresses
The Lord is asked to feed His inherited flock as in former days

expert.explanation: The petition calls the people the flock of God's heritage and asks feeding in Bashan and Gilead as of old, followed by wonders like the exodus.

expert.question: How do the nations' gestures in Micah 7:16-17 express reversal?

options.text: Their confusion gives way to a new alliance with the restored remnant
Their mourning gives way to renewed claims over Israel's inheritance
Their might gives way to silence and fear before the Lord
Their tribute gives way to demands for a share of Jerusalem's wealth

expert.explanation: Nations are confounded, cover their mouths, and lick dust, ending in fear of the Lord rather than confidence in their power.

expert.question: Which acts unfold after the question 'Who is a God like unto thee'?

options.text: Pardoning sin, showing compassion, casting sins away, and keeping ancient promises
Pardoning sin, gathering exiles, rebuilding ruined walls, and restoring former rulers
Defeating enemies, sharing plunder, renewing the priesthood, and accepting public offerings
Defeating enemies, gathering armies, removing foreign images, and establishing new borders

expert.explanation: God's pardoning character opens into compassion, sins cast away, and the performance of truth and mercy sworn to the fathers.

expert.question: Which actions show the Lord's power before Nahum calls Him a stronghold?

options.text: Parting the river, feeding the camp, guiding the armies, and halting the sun
Drying seas and rivers, shaking mountains, melting hills, and throwing down rocks
Darkening the sky, sending hail, scattering the chariots, and rescuing the captives
Flooding the fields, raising the walls, gathering the nations, and rebuilding the sanctuary

expert.explanation: Seas dry, mountains quake, hills melt, and rocks fall; the ensuing stronghold promise rests beside this depiction of divine power.

expert.question: What specific limit accompanies the Lord's patience in Nahum 1:3?

options.text: He will not hear returning captives
He will not restore the sanctuary
He will not gather the remnant
He will not acquit the wicked

expert.explanation: The same verse that names slowness to anger names great power and says the Lord will not acquit the wicked.

expert.question: How do knowledge and pursuit contrast in Nahum 1:7-8?

options.text: He knows those trusting Him while darkness pursues the judged place
He knows those ruling the city while enemies pursue the returning flock
He knows those bringing offerings while drought pursues the eastern fields
He knows those repairing walls while soldiers pursue the scattered priests

expert.explanation: The Lord knows those trusting Him; the next verse describes an overrunning flood and pursuing darkness, preserving refuge alongside judgment.
